fields.Participants: AR Clerk, Trade Account Manager, Accounting Manager
fields.Trigger: Delivery completed and accepted by government entity

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-generate of "generates government invoice" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-document of "Supporting documents compiled" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-count of "accounting/finance department" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - operational: standard operating procedures; system-enforced validation rules
Pain Points / Risks: - **Document completeness**: Government entities reject incomplete invoice packages; missing acceptance certificate or delivery receipt delays payment by weeks
System Touchpoints: - Government AR invoice generation with BIR compliance (W1966.1)
- Integration with W540 (BIR invoice) for invoice format
- Integration with W8 (AR processing) for billing cycle
Time Estimate: - 45–90 min per invoice including document compilation and submission

steps.activity: AR Clerk generates government invoice: (a) BIR-registered sales invoice or official receipt per DOC-002, (b) include: government entity TIN, BuildRight TIN, CAS permit number, contract/PO reference, delivery receipt reference, acceptance certificate reference, (c) line items: product description, quantity, unit price, total per line, (d) VAT: 12% output VAT on gross amount (unless entity is VAT-exempt per specific law), (e) EWT: indicate 1% EWT to be withheld by government entity

Supporting documents compiled: (a) signed delivery receipt, (b) acceptance certificate, (c) contract/PO copy, (d) inspection report (if applicable), (e) disbursement voucher (government payment request form — some agencies require BuildRight to prepare)

Invoice submission: (a) submit to government entity's accounting/finance department, (b) follow submission format required by specific agency (some have online portals, others require physical submission), (c) obtain acknowledgment of receipt with date stamp

fields.Frequency: Monthly collection cycle; weekly follow-up for overdue
fields.Participants: AR Clerk, Trade Account Manager, Accounting Manager
fields.Trigger: Government invoice past due; monthly collection cycle

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "accounts typically have longer collection cycle" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-escalate of "escalate to VP Store Operations for management-level follow-up" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-document of "Collection tactics for government" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - operational: standard operating procedures; system-enforced validation rules
Pain Points / Risks: - **Bureaucratic payment process**: Government payments pass through multiple approvals (receiving, inspection, accounting, finance, COA audit); each step adds days to collection cycle
System Touchpoints: - Government AR aging report (W1967.1)
- Integration with W108 (customer credit collection & escalation) for collection workflow

steps.activity: Monthly: AR Clerk generates government AR aging report: (a) by entity type (national govt, LGU, GOCC), (b) aging buckets: current, 30, 60, 90, 120+ days, (c) government accounts typically have longer collection cycle: average DSO 45–75 days vs. 30 days for trade accounts

Weekly: AR Clerk follows up on overdue government invoices: (a) 30+ days: call government accounting department, (b) 60+ days: Trade Account Manager contacts procurement officer for intervention, (c) 90+ days: escalate to VP Store Operations for management-level follow-up, (d) 120+ days: VP Legal issues formal demand letter

Collection tactics for government: (a) leverage relationship: Trade Account Manager follows up during next sales interaction, (b) pre-payment verification: ensure all required documents submitted (government won't pay without complete documentation), (c) COA (Commission on Audit) clearance: some payments require COA audit before release; ensure compliance

fields.Participants: Tax Accountant, AR Clerk, Trade Account Manager
fields.Trigger: Government entity withholds EWT on payment; quarterly BIR filing

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-record of "Government entity withholds 1% EWT on payment" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-count of "Account Manager follows up for 2307 issuance if not provided with payment" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-reconcile of "reconciles government EWT" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-381 (ensure controlled execution — Government Billing, Collection & Compliance (PA-46.3).)
- operational: periodic reconciliation against source documents
Pain Points / Risks: - **2307 collection difficulty**: Some government entities are slow to issue BIR 2307; without it, BuildRight cannot credit the withheld tax, resulting in double taxation (pay full income tax + EWT already withheld)
System Touchpoints: - EWT receivable posting on government payments (W1968.1)
- BIR 2307 tracking and reconciliation (W1968.3)
- Integration with W90 (monthly tax filing) for EWT credit application

steps.activity: Government entity withholds 1% EWT on payment: (a) government pays net of 1% EWT (e.g., PHP 100K invoice → government pays PHP 99K + issues BIR Form 2307 for PHP 1K EWT), (b) AR Clerk records: (i) cash received: PHP 99K, (ii) EWT receivable: PHP 1K, (iii) AR cleared: PHP 100K

BIR Form 2307 collection: (a) government entity issues BIR Form 2307 (Certificate of Creditable Tax Withheld at Source), (b) Trade Account Manager follows up for 2307 issuance if not provided with payment, (c) collect 2307 within 30 days of payment — required for quarterly income tax filing

Quarterly: Tax Accountant reconciles government EWT: (a) total EWT withheld by all government entities in quarter, (b) total BIR 2307 certificates collected, (c) uncollected 2307: follow-up list for Trade Account Manager, (d) credit EWT against quarterly income tax payment per BIR 1702Q

fields.Participants: Accounting Manager, Tax Accountant, Trade Account Manager, CFO

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "Accounting Manager compiles annual government sales report" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-document of "document and carry forward to next year" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-generate of "prepares government relationship report" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-381 (ensure controlled execution — Government Billing, Collection & Compliance (PA-46.3).)
- operational: periodic reconciliation against source documents
Pain Points / Risks: - **Uncollected 2307 at year-end**: If government entity hasn't issued BIR 2307 by December 31, BuildRight cannot claim EWT credit for that tax year; aggressive follow-up needed in November-December
System Touchpoints: - Annual government sales report (W1969.1)
- EWT reconciliation for annual tax filing (W1969.2)
- Integration with W9B (year-end close) for financial reporting

steps.activity: Accounting Manager compiles annual government sales report: (a) total government revenue by entity type, (b) total government sales invoices issued, (c) total EWT withheld by government entities, (d) total BIR 2307 collected, (e) total government accounts receivable balance at year-end, (f) bad debt provision for government AR

Tax Accountant reconciles government EWT for annual income tax return: (a) total EWT per BIR 2307 certificates, (b) credit against annual income tax liability per BIR 1702RT, (c) any uncollected 2307: document and carry forward to next year

Trade Account Manager prepares government relationship report: (a) active government accounts and their status, (b) contracts expiring in next year requiring renewal, (c) collection performance: average DSO by entity type, (d) pipeline for next year

fields.Participants: AR Clerk, Trade Account Manager, Credit Analyst
fields.Trigger: Institutional account purchase; monthly billing cycle

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "AR Clerk processes institutional account billing" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-collect of "collection" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System workflow notification of "contacts account directly," (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-381 (ensure controlled execution — Government Billing, Collection & Compliance (PA-46.3).)
- operational: standard operating procedures; system-enforced validation rules
Pain Points / Risks: - **NGO funding dependency**: Some NGOs depend on foreign donor funding; if donor payment delayed, NGO defaults on BuildRight payment; shorter terms or COD recommended for high-risk NGOs
System Touchpoints: - Institutional account billing through standard AR module (W1970.1)
- Integration with W8 (AR processing) and W108 (collection escalation)

steps.activity: AR Clerk processes institutional account billing: (a) standard trade billing per W8, (b) institutional accounts: schools, hospitals, churches, NGOs — processed like trade accounts with standard BIR invoice, (c) VAT: standard 12% (no special government VAT treatment), (d) EWT: may apply depending on institutional type (private entities may or may not withhold)

Collection: (a) standard collection process per W108, (b) institutional accounts: typically better payers than government but may have budget cycle constraints (schools: aligned to school year; churches: aligned to liturgical calendar; NGOs: aligned to donor funding cycles), (c) terms: Net 30 standard; Net 60 for established accounts

Overdue management: (a) standard escalation per W108, (b) for institutional accounts: Trade Account Manager contacts account directly, (c) payment plan offered for legitimate financial difficulty (common with smaller NGOs and schools)

fields.Participants: Accounting Manager, Trade Account Manager, CFO, External Auditor
fields.Trigger: Government contract with specific revenue recognition milestones

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "Accounting Manager assesses government contract revenue recognition per PFRS 15" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-review of "reviews government revenue recognition" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-381 (ensure controlled execution — Government Billing, Collection & Compliance (PA-46.3).)
- operational: Accounting Manager review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Recognition timing**: Revenue should be recognized at acceptance (not delivery or invoicing); government acceptance may lag delivery by weeks
System Touchpoints: - Revenue recognition module with milestone tracking (W1971.2)
- Integration with W487 (revenue recognition review) for PFRS 15 compliance

steps.activity: Accounting Manager assesses government contract revenue recognition per PFRS 15: (a) identify performance obligations: delivery of goods, installation services (if included), warranty, (b) transaction price: contract value less EWT, (c) allocation: allocate transaction price to each performance obligation, (d) timing: recognize revenue when (or as) performance obligation satisfied — for goods: at delivery and acceptance

Multi-delivery contracts: (a) revenue recognized per delivery milestone as each delivery is accepted by government entity, (b) partial delivery: recognize revenue for accepted portion only, (c) installation included: separate performance obligation; recognize installation revenue when installation complete

Annual: External Auditor reviews government revenue recognition: (a) sample government contracts for PFRS 15 compliance, (b) verify timing of revenue recognition (delivery acceptance vs. invoice date), (c) verify EWT treatment (net of EWT as transaction price)

fields.Participants: Tax Accountant, AR Clerk, Accounting Manager

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-validate of "verify per entity" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-report of "reporting" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-flag for investigation of "investigate per location" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-381 (ensure controlled execution — Government Billing, Collection & Compliance (PA-46.3).)
- operational: periodic reconciliation against source documents
Pain Points / Risks: - **VAT-exempt misclassification**: Incorrectly treating a government sale as VAT-exempt (or vice versa) creates BIR compliance risk; verify each government entity's VAT status
System Touchpoints: - Government VAT classification in AR module (W1972.1)
- Integration with W90 (monthly tax filing) for consolidated reporting
Time Estimate: - Absorbed in monthly tax filing cycle

steps.activity: Monthly: Tax Accountant includes government sales in VAT return: (a) government sales are generally VAT-inclusive (12% output VAT charged), (b) some government entities may be VAT-exempt per specific law (e.g., certain international organizations, diplomatic missions) — verify per entity, (c) VAT-exempt government sales reported in separate schedule of VAT return

EWT reporting: (a) total government EWT withheld reported in quarterly income tax return (BIR 1702Q), (b) annual reconciliation in annual income tax return (BIR 1702RT), (c) uncredited EWT from prior years carried forward

Local Business Tax (LBT): (a) government sales included in gross receipts for LBT computation per LGU, (b) some LGUs offer LBT incentives for businesses with significant government contracts — investigate per location

fields.Frequency: Monthly aging review; quarterly provision assessment
fields.Trigger: Month-end close; quarterly bad debt review

workflows.name: Government Account Aging & Bad Debt Provision

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-review of "reviews government AR aging" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-log of "methodology" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-collect of "collection rate assumption still valid?" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-381 (ensure controlled execution — Government Billing, Collection & Compliance (PA-46.3).)
- operational: Accounting Manager review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Extended aging**: Government accounts may age 120–180+ days but still be collectible (bureaucratic delay, not credit risk); do not prematurely write off
System Touchpoints: - Government AR aging report (W1973.1)
- Bad debt provision calculation (W1973.2)
- Integration with W81 (bad debt write-off) for actual write-off processing

steps.activity: Monthly: Accounting Manager reviews government AR aging: (a) total government AR balance, (b) aging distribution: current, 30, 60, 90, 120, 180+ days, (c) compare to prior month: is government AR improving or deteriorating?, (d) flag accounts > 90 days for Trade Account Manager follow-up

Quarterly: Credit Analyst assesses bad debt provision for government accounts: (a) historical collection rate: government accounts collect ~95–98% eventually (very low actual write-off), (b) provision methodology: lower provision rate than trade accounts due to lower default risk, (c) specific provision for accounts > 180 days: assess collectibility per account, (d) accounts > 1 year: specific assessment — is there a legitimate reason for non-payment (dispute, documentation issue, budget reallocation)?

Annual: CFO reviews government bad debt provisioning policy: (a) is 95–98% collection rate assumption still valid?, (b) any systemic collection issues (e.g., specific government entity consistently paying late), (c) adjust provisioning policy if needed
